title: Psalms Chapter 64 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 64 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 64 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 64.

questions.question: Who is the Psalm of Psalms 64 attributed to?
questions.correctAnswer: David
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:1 identifies the Psalm as 'A Psalm of David.'

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask God to preserve his life from?
questions.correctAnswer: Fear of the enemy
questions.explanation: In Psalms 64:1, the psalmist prays to be preserved from 'fear of the enemy.'

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist asks God to hear his voice in prayer.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:1 says, 'Hear my voice, O God, in my prayer.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 64:2, from what does the psalmist ask to be hidden?
questions.correctAnswer: Secret counsel of the wicked
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:2 states, 'Hide me from the secret counsel of the wicked.'

questions.question: True or False: The workers of iniquity are mentioned in Psalms 64:2 as being involved in an insurrection.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:2 refers to 'the insurrection of the workers of iniquity.'

questions.question: What do the wicked do with their tongues, according to Psalms 64:3?
options: Whet their tongue like a sword
questions.correctAnswer: Whet their tongue like a sword
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:3 says they 'whet their tongue like a sword.'

questions.question: Which weapon is mentioned in Psalms 64:3 as being bent to shoot bitter words?
questions.correctAnswer: Bows
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:3 mentions 'bend their bows to shoot their arrows, even bitter words.'

questions.question: True or False: The enemies shoot their arrows openly and fear being seen.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:4 says they 'shoot in secret' and 'fear not.'

questions.question: Who are the targets of the secret shots mentioned in Psalms 64:4?
questions.correctAnswer: The perfect
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:4 states they 'shoot in secret at the perfect.'

questions.question: What do the workers of iniquity encourage themselves in, according to Psalms 64:5?
questions.correctAnswer: An evil matter
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:5 says, 'They encourage themselves in an evil matter.'

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 64:5, the workers of iniquity believe that nobody will see their snares.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:5 says they say, 'Who shall see them?'.

questions.question: What do the workers of iniquity do, as described in Psalms 64:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Search out iniquities diligently
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:6 says, 'They search out iniquities; they accomplish a diligent search.'

questions.question: What part of the workers of iniquity is described as deep in Psalms 64:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Heart and inward thought
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:6 states, 'both the inward thought of every one of them, and the heart, is deep.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 64, what does God do to the workers of iniquity?
options: Shoots at them with an arrow
questions.correctAnswer: Shoots at them with an arrow
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:7 says, 'But God shall shoot at them with an arrow; suddenly shall they be wounded.'

questions.question: In what order do these events occur in Psalms 64? A) The workers of iniquity secretly plot. B) The psalmist asks God to hear his prayer. C) God wounds the workers of iniquity. D) The workers of iniquity shoot bitter words.
questions.correctAnswer: B, A, D, C
questions.explanation: First, the psalmist asks God to hear his prayer (verse 1), then the wicked secretly plot (verse 2), next they shoot bitter words (verse 3), and finally God wounds them (verse 7).

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 64 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 64 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 64:5, what do the workers of iniquity do in secret?
options: They encourage themselves in an evil matter and lay snares privily
questions.correctAnswer: They encourage themselves in an evil matter and lay snares privily
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:5 states that the wicked encourage themselves in evil and commune about laying snares in secret, showing their deliberate planning of harm.

questions.question: What does Psalms 64:6 reveal about the thoughts and hearts of the workers of iniquity?
options: Their inward thoughts and hearts are deep and they diligently search out iniquities
Their hearts are pure and full of love
Their thoughts are shallow and careless
questions.correctAnswer: Their inward thoughts and hearts are deep and they diligently search out iniquities
questions.explanation: Verse 6 shows that the wicked carefully and deeply plan their evil acts, indicating the seriousness of their intentions.

questions.question: How does Psalms 64:7 describe God's response to the wicked's secret plans?
options: God will shoot them with an arrow and wound them suddenly
God will hide them from harm
questions.correctAnswer: God will shoot them with an arrow and wound them suddenly
questions.explanation: Verse 7 clearly states that God will strike the wicked swiftly and decisively, countering their evil schemes.

questions.question: What consequence does Psalms 64:8 say will happen to the wicked because of their own tongues?
options: Their tongues will cause harm to themselves, and all who see them will flee
Their tongues will bring them peace
Their tongues will convince the righteous
Their tongues will be silent forever
questions.correctAnswer: Their tongues will cause harm to themselves, and all who see them will flee
questions.explanation: Verse 8 teaches that the wicked's own words will backfire, leading others to avoid them out of fear or disgust.

questions.question: What does Psalms 64:9 say will be the reaction of people after seeing God's justice on the wicked?
options: All men shall fear and declare the work of God, wisely considering His deeds
They will rejoice in the wicked's success
They will forget about God's justice
questions.correctAnswer: All men shall fear and declare the work of God, wisely considering His deeds
questions.explanation: According to verse 9, witnessing God's justice causes people to fear Him and thoughtfully acknowledge His works.

questions.question: In Psalms 64:10, what is said about the righteous and those upright in heart?
options: They shall be glad in the LORD, trust in Him, and glory
They shall be fearful and doubtful
They shall hide from their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be glad in the LORD, trust in Him, and glory
questions.explanation: Verse 10 emphasizes the joy, trust, and pride the righteous and upright have in their relationship with God.

questions.question: How does Psalms 64:5-6 help us understand the nature of evil intentions in others?
options: Evil intentions are deeply planned and secretive, with deliberate searching for ways to harm
Evil intentions are always obvious and shallow
Evil intentions come from ignorance rather than planning
Evil intentions cannot harm the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: Evil intentions are deeply planned and secretive, with deliberate searching for ways to harm
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 6 describe the wicked as encouraging themselves in evil and diligently searching out iniquities, revealing their calculated secret plans.

questions.question: What does Psalms 64:7-8 teach about God's justice and the ultimate fate of the wicked?
options: God will strike the wicked suddenly, causing their own words to condemn them and causing others to flee
The wicked will triumph over the righteous
God will remain silent about the wicked's deeds
questions.correctAnswer: God will strike the wicked suddenly, causing their own words to condemn them and causing others to flee
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 show that God actively punishes the wicked with sudden judgment, and their self-condemning tongues make others avoid them.

questions.question: If a fellow believer is troubled by secret attacks from others, what biblical truth from Psalms 64:5-8 applies?
options: God sees the secret plans and will judge the wicked suddenly, causing their own words to bring their downfall
The believer should retaliate with similar secret plans
The believer should ignore prayer and rely on their own strength
The believer must isolate themselves from all people
questions.correctAnswer: God sees the secret plans and will judge the wicked suddenly, causing their own words to bring their downfall
questions.explanation: These verses assure that God is aware of secret evil and will swiftly bring justice, encouraging believers to trust Him rather than seek revenge.

questions.question: According to Psalms 64:9, how does witnessing God's work affect people's hearts and minds?
options: It causes fear and thoughtful declaration of God's deeds
It causes confusion about right and wrong
It causes people to ignore God's justice
questions.correctAnswer: It causes fear and thoughtful declaration of God's deeds
questions.explanation: Verse 9 explains that seeing God's justice leads to reverence and wise reflection on His actions.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 64:6 suggests that the wicked are careless and do not think deeply about their evil plans.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:6 states that the wicked accomplish a diligent search and that their inward thoughts and hearts are deep, showing careful planning.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 64:10, the righteous will find gladness and glory in trusting the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 10 clearly says that the righteous will be glad, trust in the LORD, and glory, highlighting the blessedness of faith.

questions.question: What does Psalms 64:8 imply about the power of words spoken by the wicked?
options: Their own tongues cause their downfall and cause others to flee
Their words bring peace and reconciliation
questions.correctAnswer: Their own tongues cause their downfall and cause others to flee
questions.explanation: Verse 8 teaches that the wicked's own words become their ruin and drive people away from them.

questions.question: How does Psalms 64:7-9 encourage believers in dealing with enemies who plot secretly?
options: Trust that God will suddenly wound the wicked and that His justice will cause reverence
Live in constant fear without hope
Ignore prayer and rely on human wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Trust that God will suddenly wound the wicked and that His justice will cause reverence
questions.explanation: Verses 7-9 assure believers that God actively judges the wicked and that His works inspire fear and respect, encouraging trust in Him.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 64:5 indicates that the wicked openly boast about their evil plans to everyone.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 5 shows that the wicked lay their snares privily and ask 'Who shall see them?', indicating secretive behavior, not open boasting.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 64 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 64.

questions.question: According to Psalms 64:9, what is the reaction of all men when they see the work of God?
questions.correctAnswer: They shall fear
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:9 states that 'all men shall fear, and shall declare the work of God,' indicating that fear is the immediate reaction upon witnessing God's work.

questions.question: Psalms 64:10 mentions the righteous will be glad and trust in whom?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:10 clearly says 'The righteous shall be glad in the LORD, and shall trust in him,' emphasizing reliance on God.

questions.question: What do 'all the upright in heart' do according to Psalms 64:10?
questions.correctAnswer: Glory
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:10 states that 'all the upright in heart shall glory,' highlighting their joyful praise.

questions.question: The phrase 'declare the work of God' in Psalms 64:9 suggests what kind of activity?
questions.correctAnswer: Proclaiming God's deeds
questions.explanation: To 'declare the work of God' implies openly proclaiming or making known God's actions, as per Psalms 64:9.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of fearing God and declaring His work, similar to Psalms 64:9?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 33:8
questions.explanation: Psalm 33:8 says, 'Let all the earth fear the LORD: let all the inhabitants of the world stand in awe of him,' which parallels the theme in Psalms 64:9 of fearing God and acknowledging His work.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Psalms 64:3 with the imagery of tongues as swords and bows shooting arrows?
questions.correctAnswer: Simile
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:3 uses similes comparing tongues to swords and bows shooting arrows to describe sharp, hurtful speech, illustrating the literary device of simile.

questions.question: In Psalms 64:7, how does God respond to the wicked according to the text?
options: God shoots at them with an arrow
questions.correctAnswer: God shoots at them with an arrow
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:7 states 'But God shall shoot at them with an arrow; suddenly shall they be wounded,' indicating divine retribution.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'fear' in Psalms 64:1 primarily convey in its original context?
questions.correctAnswer: Reverence and awe
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'fear' (yirah) often conveys reverence and awe towards God, not just terror, consistent with Psalms 64:1's plea for preservation from enemies.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of trusting in God amidst enemies as found in Psalms 64:10?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 15:13
questions.explanation: Romans 15:13 encourages believers to trust in God for hope and joy, echoing the trust and gladness in the LORD described in Psalms 64:10.

questions.question: What does Psalms 64:6 reveal about the nature of the wicked's thoughts?
options: Their hearts are deep and their thoughts inward
questions.correctAnswer: Their hearts are deep and their thoughts inward
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:6 explains that the wicked search diligently and their inward thoughts and hearts are deep, indicating complexity in their evil plans.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 64:5 indicates that the wicked believe their secret plans will remain unseen.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:5 says, 'they commune of laying snares privily; they say, Who shall see them?' showing their confidence that their plans remain hidden.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 64:8, those who see the wicked will confront and capture them.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:8 states 'all that see them shall flee away,' indicating that witnesses of the wicked's downfall will flee, not confront.

questions.question: How does Psalms 64:4 describe the wicked's attack on the 'perfect'?
options: They shoot suddenly and without fear
questions.correctAnswer: They shoot suddenly and without fear
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:4 says, 'suddenly do they shoot at him, and fear not,' describing a sudden and fearless attack.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage also discusses the theme of righteous rejoicing and trusting in the LORD, similar to Psalms 64:10?
questions.correctAnswer: Nehemiah 8:10
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 8:10 says, 'the joy of the LORD is your strength,' reflecting the righteous gladness and trust in God seen in Psalms 64:10.

questions.question: What is the primary reason given in Psalms 64:9 for why men will fear and declare God's work?
options: They shall wisely consider His doing
They desire to be seen by others
questions.correctAnswer: They shall wisely consider His doing
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:9 explains the fear and declaration come because men 'shall wisely consider of his doing,' showing understanding leads to reverence.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 64 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 64 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What is the psalmist's request in Psalms 64:1 regarding his prayer to God?
options: Preserve my life from fear of the enemy
Reveal the secrets of the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: Preserve my life from fear of the enemy
questions.explanation: In Psalms 64:1, the psalmist asks God to hear his voice in prayer and to preserve his life from fear of the enemy, showing a plea for protection.

questions.question: According to Psalms 64:2, from what is the psalmist asking God to hide him?
options: The secret counsel of the wicked and insurrection of workers of iniquity
The open attacks of the enemy
questions.correctAnswer: The secret counsel of the wicked and insurrection of workers of iniquity
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:2 specifically requests hiding from the secret counsel of the wicked and the insurrection of workers of iniquity, emphasizing the hidden dangers from evil plotting.

questions.question: In Psalms 64:3, what metaphor is used to describe the weapons of the wicked?
options: Tongue like a sword and bows to shoot arrows of bitter words
questions.correctAnswer: Tongue like a sword and bows to shoot arrows of bitter words
questions.explanation: The verse uses a metaphor of the tongue as a sword and bows shooting arrows, representing verbal attacks and slander by the wicked (Psalms 64:3).

questions.question: What characteristic of the wicked's attack is emphasized in Psalms 64:4?
options: They shoot in secret at the perfect without fear
questions.correctAnswer: They shoot in secret at the perfect without fear
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:4 describes the wicked shooting secretly at the perfect and doing so fearlessly, highlighting their covert and bold malice.

questions.question: What does Psalms 64:5 reveal about the mindset of the wicked?
options: They encourage themselves in evil and secretly lay snares, asking who will see them
They fear the judgment of God
questions.correctAnswer: They encourage themselves in evil and secretly lay snares, asking who will see them
questions.explanation: Verse 5 shows the wicked's confidence in their evil plans and their secret plotting, reflecting moral blindness and pride (Psalms 64:5).

questions.question: How does Psalms 64:6 describe the thoroughness of the wicked in planning their iniquities?
options: They search out iniquities with diligent search, and their inward thought and heart is deep
questions.correctAnswer: They search out iniquities with diligent search, and their inward thought and heart is deep
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:6 emphasizes the wicked’s careful, deep planning and intention in their sinful activities.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Psalms 64:7 by God's sudden wounding of the wicked?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice and sovereignty
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:7 shows God acting justly and sovereignly by suddenly wounding the wicked, demonstrating His control over evil and enforcement of justice.

questions.question: According to Psalms 64:8, what consequence befalls the wicked because of their own words?
options: Their tongues fall upon themselves causing others to flee
questions.correctAnswer: Their tongues fall upon themselves causing others to flee
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:8 teaches that the wicked’s words bring their own downfall, resulting in others fleeing from them, illustrating the self-destructive power of evil speech.

questions.question: What is the universal human response to God's work as described in Psalms 64:9?
options: All men shall fear and declare the work of God, wisely considering His doing
questions.correctAnswer: All men shall fear and declare the work of God, wisely considering His doing
questions.explanation: Verse 9 reveals that God's work causes reverent fear and declaration among all men, showing recognition of His power and wisdom (Psalms 64:9).

questions.question: What is the attitude of the righteous toward the LORD according to Psalms 64:10?
options: They are glad, trust in Him, and glory in their upright hearts
They rely on their own strength
questions.correctAnswer: They are glad, trust in Him, and glory in their upright hearts
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:10 describes the righteous rejoicing and trusting in the LORD, expressing joy and confidence grounded in uprightness.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight about divine justice and human evil is taught by Psalms 64:5-6 and 64:7?
options: God thoroughly knows and judges the secret evil plans of the wicked with swift justice
Human evil is beyond God’s control
God is indifferent to secret sins
questions.correctAnswer: God thoroughly knows and judges the secret evil plans of the wicked with swift justice
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 describe the wicked’s secret plotting and deep evil thoughts, while verse 7 shows God's swift justice, revealing His omniscient judgment over hidden sins.

questions.question: What combined teaching about the power of speech and its consequences is found in Psalms 64:3 and 64:8?
options: The wicked use harmful words as weapons, but these words ultimately bring ruin upon themselves
Words are only for blessing others
The righteous are destroyed by their own words
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked use harmful words as weapons, but these words ultimately bring ruin upon themselves
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:3 uses the metaphor of tongues as swords shooting arrows; 64:8 states that the wicked’s tongues cause their own downfall, emphasizing the destructive power of sinful speech.

questions.question: How does the combination of Psalms 64:1 and 64:10 express the relationship between fear and trust in God?
options: The psalmist asks for deliverance from fear and expresses that the righteous trust and rejoice in God
Fear is encouraged as a permanent state
The righteous rely only on their own strength
questions.correctAnswer: The psalmist asks for deliverance from fear and expresses that the righteous trust and rejoice in God
questions.explanation: Verse 1 shows a plea for protection from fear, while verse 10 depicts the righteous as glad and trusting in the LORD, highlighting salvation from fear through faith.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that secret evil plans always go unnoticed and unpunished. What does Psalms 64:2-7 teach about God's knowledge and judgment of hidden sins?
options: God is aware of secret counsels of the wicked and will suddenly wound them with justice
questions.correctAnswer: God is aware of secret counsels of the wicked and will suddenly wound them with justice
questions.explanation: Verses 2-7 reveal that though the wicked plot secretly, God knows their hearts and thoughts and will act decisively to bring justice, refuting sceptics denying divine justice over hidden sins.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is most clearly illustrated by His action described in Psalms 64:9, where all men fear and declare His work?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s wisdom and power
questions.explanation: Psalms 64:9 shows that all men fear and acknowledge God's work, which reflects His wisdom in governance and power over all creation.
